quarterly_data.signal: Second-quarter 2026 earnings release (8-K Exhibit 99.1): U.S. total revenue increased 11% to $2.06 billion and revenue outside the U.S. increased 14% to $1.28 billion. Product revenue: TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO $2,497.2 million (Q2 2025: $2,551.1 million), ALYFTREK $573.6 million ($156.8 million), other CF products $137.1 million ($193.7 million). The full-year 2026 revenue guidance of $13.1 billion to $13.2 billion was raised from $12.95 billion to $13.1 billion previously; GAAP combined R&D, AIPR&D and SG&A guidance of $6.3 billion to $6.45 billion was reiterated, and guidance includes an immaterial cost impact from tariffs in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: U.S. $2.06 billion (+11%); ex-U.S. $1.28 billion (+14%); TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO $2,497.2 million; ALYFTREK $573.6 million; prior guidance $12.95 billion to $13.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Vertex presented Phase 3 data at the European Cystic Fibrosis Conference for ALYFTREK in children 2 to 5 years of age: 65% of children, including those with F/F and F/MF genotypes, reached carrier sweat chloride levels of <30 mmol/L, with a mean reduction in sweat chloride of 9.6 mmol/L from a baseline on TRIKAFTA; ALYFTREK was generally safe and well tolerated. In Q2 2026 Vertex secured ALYFTREK reimbursement in four additional countries, including Spain, bringing the total to 25, and signed a letter of intent with the Pan-Canadian Pharmaceutical Alliance for reimbursement for eligible patients 6 years and older in Canada.
quarterly_data.figure: 65% of children 2 to 5 reached sweat chloride <30 mmol/L; mean reduction 9.6 mmol/L from TRIKAFTA baseline; ALYFTREK reimbursed in 25 countries

quarterly_data.signal: CASGEVY is approved in 39 countries across North America, Europe and the Middle East. With the U.S. FDA approval in children 2 years of age and older with SCD or TDT, approximately 5,500 patients may be eligible for treatment with CASGEVY for the first time. In May Vertex secured reimbursement for CASGEVY for eligible patients 12 years and older with SCD or TDT in Germany, and it continues to advance preclinical assets for gentler conditioning toward clinical trials, which could broaden the eligible patient population.
quarterly_data.figure: approved in 39 countries; approximately 5,500 newly eligible U.S. patients ages 2+

quarterly_data.signal: During the second quarter Health Canada accepted Vertex's new drug submission for suzetrigine for moderate-to-severe acute pain, and review is underway. Twenty-three states provide coverage for JOURNAVX via Medicaid. In neuropathic pain, Vertex is on track to complete enrollment in a Phase 2 study of VX-993 in people with diabetic peripheral neuropathy by the end of 2026, and continues to advance toward clinical trials preclinical assets that inhibit NaV1.7 for use alone or in combination with a NaV1.8 inhibitor.
quarterly_data.figure: Health Canada review of suzetrigine underway; Twenty-three states provide Medicaid coverage; VX-993 Phase 2 DPN enrollment on track to complete by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: The povetacicept BLA for accelerated approval in adults with IgAN (PDUFA November 30, 2026) is supported by positive data from a pre-specified Week 36 interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 RAINIER trial; if approved, povetacicept will become the first commercialized therapy in Vertex's nephrology pillar. AGLOW, the VX-407 ADPKD study, is a 26-patient, single-arm, 52-week Phase 2 proof-of-concept study evaluating height-adjusted total kidney volume (htTKV) in patients with a subset of PKD1 variants estimated at up to approximately 30,000 (or up to approximately 10%) of the overall ADPKD population.
quarterly_data.figure: RAINIER Week 36 interim analysis; AGLOW 26 patients, 52 weeks; up to approximately 30,000 (up to approximately 10%) of ADPKD patients

quarterly_data.signal: In myotonic dystrophy type 1, Vertex recently completed enrollment and continues to dose people in the multiple ascending dose portion of the GALILEO global Phase 1/2 trial of VX-670, an oligonucleotide linked to a cyclic peptide; the study assesses safety and preliminary efficacy by change from baseline in the splicing index on muscle biopsy as well as vHOT and QMT score, and Vertex is on track to complete dosing and share results in the second half of 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: GALILEO Phase 1/2 MAD enrollment complete; results in the second half of 2026
